correctness.rationale: Direct plane Hasse-Witt coefficient extraction gives diagonal coefficient polynomials A_m,B_m,D_m; a uniform modular ODE proves A_m=binom(4m,2m)(a²−4)^m and D_m=[binom(4m,m)/binom(2m,m)](a²−4)^m B_m. ODE uniqueness uses 0≤r<K< p and 2N−K<p, valid for all three pairs. B_m has degree m<p, nonzero at a=±2 and simple roots by ODE differentiation. Thus stable semilinear rank is 3/1 and a-number is 0/2. The ordinary elliptic quotient and prime-to-p Prym splitting imply the superspecial Prym claim. All fifteen test primes independently matched coefficient identities, diagonal entries and squarefreeness. Finite tests are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected bielliptic Picard geometry and Ceresa-cycle literature establishes the family and Prym but not this explicit reduced arithmetic nonordinary divisor, the nontrivial factorization and its simple-root count. The general Hasse-Witt coefficient formula is acknowledged, not claimed new; a published blanket ordinarity claim has a direct smooth counterexample and does not imply the correct new classification. The source material of the earlier general Hasse matrix and complex hypergeometric Shimura uniformization was available only in abstract, leaving recorded priority risk. Multiple semantic published-finding corpus searches and own accessible historical finding-claim comparisons found no direct cover; absence alone does not prove uniqueness.

value.rationale: The discriminant-six Prym family is a natural one-dimensional arithmetic moduli locus. The theorem gives all nonordinary parameters for every prime p≡1 (mod6), their exact reduced multiplicity-one support, strict Hasse determinant multiplicity two, the stable p-rank and Cartier a-number for every smooth curve, and superspecial Prym surfaces exactly on the exceptional locus. This is a structural classification in unbounded characteristic, not a fixed small-prime point count, unmotivated slice or mere algorithmic recomputation.
